inclusion.I1: English language empirical studies with original data
inclusion.I2: Functional MRI study in humans assessing drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with a clear visual cue component (visual-only or multimodal designs that include visual cues)

exclusion.E2: Cue-reactivity paradigms with no visual cue component (e.g., purely gustatory, olfactory, or tactile designs)

inclusion.I3: Functional MRI study assessing drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with a clear visual cue component (visual-only or multimodal designs that include visual cues)
inclusion.I4: At least one analysis involving a within-participant contrast of drug cues>control stimuli or natural reward-related cues>control stimuli

I5.Whole-brain or small-volume-corrected ev: at least one qualifying analysis must be a group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical result, reported as either whole-brain or small-volume-corrected.

inclusion.I6: It is acceptable for qualifying voxelwise results to be reported in tables of coordinates, figures, or supplementary materials when the main text clearly indicates those results are available.
inclusion.I7: Reporting of participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software is preferred; missing one or more of these details alone should not exclude an otherwise qualifying study.

exclusion.E3: Studies that report only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses with no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected result.
exclusion.E4: Studies that report only seed-based connectivity, effective connectivity (e.g., PPI, DCM), or resting-state analyses (e.g., ICA, PLE, Hurst exponents) without also reporting a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected).
exclusion.E5: Studies that report only between-group contrasts or interactions (e.g., subgroup vs subgroup, patient vs control) without an accompanying qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast.
exclusion.E6: Non-empirical papers (e.g., reviews, meta-analyses, methods-only, simulations) without original human fMRI data.

inclusion.GLOBAL_I1: Voxelwise task evidence- The analysis must be a group-level, univariate task-evoked voxelwise map (typically whole-brain; small-volume-corrected maps are acceptable). Between-group contrasts/interactions are acceptable when they compare a qualifying cue-reactivity effect across groups.
inclusion.GLOBAL_I2: ROI exception for benchmark compatibility- ROI-focused analyses may be included only when they provide stereotactic coordinates for a qualifying visual cue-reactivity contrast.
inclusion.GLOBAL_I3: Contrast or analysis must be relevant to reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

exclusion.GLOBAL_E1: ROI analyses that do not provide stereotactic coordinates for a qualifying cue-reactivity contrast.
exclusion.GLOBAL_E2: Seed-based connectivity, effective connectivity (e.g., PPI, DCM), or resting-state analyses (e.g., ICA, PLE, Hurst exponents)
exclusion.GLOBAL_E3: Analyses on non-appetitive cue contrasts, or regulation/control contrasts (e.g., reappraisal/decrease/increase, go/no-go) without a qualifying cue-reactivity contrast.

inclusion.POOLED_CUE_REACTIVITY_I1: Analyses must be on a task measuring drug OR natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (example tasks: Drug cue reactivity; Food cue reactivity; Sexual cue reactivity; monetary reward cue tasks).
inclusion.POOLED_CUE_REACTIVITY_I2: The analysis/contrast must index appetitive cue reactivity versus a valid comparator condition (e.g., neutral, non-reward/non-drug, low-level baseline, or matched control cues; examples: Drug cues>neutral cues, Alcohol cues>non-alcoholic beverage cues, Food cues>neutral/non-food cues).

exclusion.POOLED_CUE_REACTIVITY_E1: Exclude analyses where cue-reactivity cannot be identified at the analysis/contrast level (e.g., generic pooled group maps with no explicit qualifying cue contrast).

inclusion.NATURAL_REWARD_CUE_REACTIVITY_I1: Analyses must explicitly involve NATURAL reward-related visual cue-reactivity at the analysis/contrast level (e.g., food, sexual/erotic, social, monetary/gaming reward cues).
inclusion.NATURAL_REWARD_CUE_REACTIVITY_I2: The analysis/contrast must measure natural reward-related cue reactivity versus a valid comparator condition (e.g., neutral, non-reward, low-level baseline, or matched control cues).

exclusion.NATURAL_REWARD_CUE_REACTIVITY_E1: Drug cue contrasts (e.g., Drug cues>neutral cues) should not be included in this annotation
exclusion.NATURAL_REWARD_CUE_REACTIVITY_E2: Exclude mixed or ambiguous analyses where natural-reward and drug-cue effects are not separable at the reported contrast/map level (e.g., generic group maps in mixed-task studies without an explicit natural-reward contrast).

inclusion.DRUG_CUE_REACTIVITY_I1: Analyses must explicitly involve drug-related visual cue-reactivity at the analysis/contrast level (example tasks: smoking, alcohol, cannabis, cocaine cue reactivity).
inclusion.DRUG_CUE_REACTIVITY_I2: The analysis/contrast must measure drug-related cue reactivity versus a valid comparator condition (e.g., neutral, non-drug, low-level baseline, or matched control cues; examples: Drug cues>neutral cues, Alcohol cues>non-alcoholic beverage cues).

exclusion.DRUG_CUE_REACTIVITY_E1: Analyses on natural reward-related cue contrasts (e.g., Food cues>neutral cues) should not be included in this annotation
exclusion.DRUG_CUE_REACTIVITY_E2: Exclude mixed or ambiguous analyses where drug-cue effects are not separable at the reported contrast/map level.
